ing: such as linguica or kielbasa, sliced
st: Drain the soaked beans and rinse them well.
Cook the bacon in a large heavy pot over medium heat for 6 minutes until the fat renders.
Add the pork shoulder and ribs and brown for 8 minutes. Remove half the meat if the pot is crowded.
Stir in the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the beans, [[8 cups]] water and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer, partly covered.
Simmer 90 minutes, skimming foam and stirring now and then, until the beans are soft.
Add the sliced sausage and simmer 30 more minutes until the pork is tender and the broth is thick. Mash a few beans against the pot to thicken it.
Season with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and pepper, remove the bay leaves, and serve with [[3 cups]] cooked rice and orange slices.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and lightly grease a mini muffin pan or line a tray.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] milk, [[0.33 cup]] oil and [[1 tsp]] salt in a saucepan until just boiling.
Put [[2 cups]] tapioca flour in a bowl and pour the hot milk mix over it. Stir until you have a sticky dough, then cool 10 minutes.
Mix in the eggs one at a time until smooth, then the cheeses.
Knead briefly in the bowl. The dough will be stretchy and sticky.
Scoop or roll into 24 balls about 1.5 inches wide, wetting your hands if it sticks.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and lightly golden.
Cool for 5 minutes and serve warm.
Simmer the chicken in [[3 cups]] stock for 20 minutes until cooked to 165°F (74°C). Lift out and reserve the stock.
Shred the chicken finely with two forks.
Cook the onion and garlic in [[2 tbsp]] butter for 4 minutes, then mix in the chicken, [[4 oz]] cream cheese, parsley, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and pepper. Chill.
Measure [[2 cups]] of the stock into a pot with [[1 tsp]] salt and bring to a boil.
Add [[2 cups]] flour all at once and stir hard over low heat for 3 minutes until a smooth dough pulls from the pot. Cool until warm.
Take a golf-ball piece of dough, press it into a cup in your palm, and add a spoonful of filling.
Pinch the dough closed and shape into a teardrop. Repeat for 12 pieces.
Dip each in the beaten eggs, then coat in [[1.5 cups]] breadcrumbs.
Heat [[4 cups]] oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry 3 or 4 at a time for 4 minutes until deep gold.
Drain on paper towels and cool a few minutes before serving.

ing: firm, such as cod or halibut, in large chunks
dende oil; or olive oil plus 1 tsp paprika
st: Toss the fish with the juice of [[2 limes]], [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a wide pot. Soften the garlic for 30 seconds.
Layer half the onion, tomato and pepper in the pot, then the fish, then the remaining vegetables and half the cilantro.
Pour the coconut milk over the top and drizzle with [[2 tbsp]] palm oil.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes. Do not stir; shake the pot gently instead.
Check that the fish flakes easily, then season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Scatter the remaining cilantro on top and serve with white rice.

ing: top sirloin cap, fat cap on; or top sirloin
st: Take the meat out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking.
Cut the roast into 1.5-inch thick steaks across the grain, keeping fat on each.
Score the fat in a crosshatch pattern.
Rub the steaks with [[4 cloves]] garlic, [[2 tbsp]] oil and pepper, then cover generously with [[2 tbsp]] coarse salt.
Heat a grill or cast-iron skillet to high. Sear the fat side first for 3 minutes until crisp.
Sear the meaty sides 3 to 4 minutes each for medium-rare, or until 145°F (63°C).
Rest the meat 5 minutes and slice thinly against the grain.
Serve with [[2 cups]] farofa and vinagrete.

ing: for the dough, dende oil, optional
st: Rub the soaked peas between your hands to loosen the skins, then rinse until they float away. Drain well.
Blend the peas with half the onion and [[1 tsp]] salt, adding a splash of water, into a thick fluffy paste.
Whip the batter by hand for 3 minutes to add air, which makes the fritters light.
Make the filling by cooking the remaining onion, garlic, chili, shrimp and tomato in [[2 tbsp]] palm oil for 8 minutes.
Season the filling with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and add the cilantro.
Heat [[4 cups]] oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pot.
Drop in oval spoonfuls of batter and fry for 4 minutes per side until deep brown. Drain.
Split each fritter open and fill with the shrimp mixture.

ing: toasted manioc flour, farinha de mandioca
st: Cook the diced bacon in a large skillet over medium heat for 5 minutes until crisp. Remove it, leaving the fat.
Add [[2 tbsp]] butter and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Push the onion aside, add the eggs, and scramble them for 1 minute.
Stir in the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter.
Add [[1.5 cups]] cassava flour a little at a time, stirring constantly for 4 minutes until toasted and golden.
Fold in the bacon, parsley and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Serve warm as a side to grilled meat or beans.
Finely dice the tomatoes, discarding the seeds and juice so the salsa is not watery.
Dice the onion and bell pepper to the same small size.
Combine the vegetables in a bowl.
Add [[3 tbsp]] vinegar, [[3 tbsp]] olive oil, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Stir in the parsley and toss.
Rest 15 minutes so the flavors blend, then taste and adjust the salt.

ing: for the dough, plus 4 cups for frying
st: Mix [[3 cups]] flour with [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add [[2 tbsp]] oil, [[1 tbsp]] vinegar and [[0.5 cup]] warm water, adding more water a spoon at a time as needed.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth, then rest the dough, covered, for 30 minutes.
Cook the beef and onion in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes, until the beef reaches 160°F (71°C). Add the garlic, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and pepper.
Drain the filling and cool completely.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into 12 rectangles about 4 by 6 inches.
Place a spoonful of beef and a pinch of cheese on half of each rectangle.
Fold over and press the edges closed with a fork to seal tightly.
Heat [[4 cups]] oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry the pastries 2 or 3 at a time for 3 minutes per side until blistered and gold.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
Butter a plate and your hands lightly.
Combine the condensed milk, [[3 tbsp]] cocoa, [[1 tbsp]] butter and a pinch of salt in a nonstick saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for 10 to 12 minutes.
The mixture is ready when a spoon dragged across the bottom shows the pan for 2 seconds before it closes.
Pour onto the buttered plate and cool for 20 minutes until firm enough to handle.
Roll into 16 small balls with buttered hands.
Roll each ball in [[0.75 cup]] sprinkles and place in mini paper cups.
Run the açaí packets under warm water for 20 seconds, then break each into a few pieces.
Add the açaí, frozen banana and [[0.33 cup]] milk to a blender.
Blend on low, pushing down with a tamper or spoon, until thick like soft ice cream.
Add a splash more milk only if the blender stalls.
Scoop into a chilled bowl.
Top with [[0.33 cup]] granola, sliced banana, strawberries and a drizzle of [[1 tbsp]] honey.
Eat immediately before it melts.

ing: cut into 8 wedges, white pith trimmed
optional; for a no-alcohol version use lime soda
st: Cut the lime into wedges and remove the white center pith to avoid bitterness.
Put the wedges and [[2 tsp]] sugar into a sturdy short glass.
Muddle firmly 10 to 15 seconds to release the juice and oils.
Pour in [[2 fl oz]] cachaça, or use the alcohol-free swap.
Fill the glass with [[1 cup]] crushed ice.
Stir well to dissolve the sugar and serve with a short straw.
Wash the strawberries, grapes, mango and pineapple under cold running water. Dry the pineapple and mango rinds, then peel them on a clean board.
Squeeze the juice of two oranges through a sieve into a large bowl, about [[0.75 cup]]. Stir in [[3 tbsp]] sugar until it dissolves; this syrup keeps the fruit fresh.
Cut the pineapple, mango and papaya into 2 cm cubes, removing the papaya seeds. Cut the strawberries in half, and slice the third orange into segments free of pith.
Drop the cut fruit into the juice as you go. The acid stops browning, so the bowl stays bright and the flavors begin to blend.
Stir in the grapes and passion fruit pulp if using. Cover the bowl and chill for 1 hour so the juices meld and the flavors deepen.
Just before serving, peel and slice the bananas into rounds and fold them in gently so they do not turn mushy. Taste and add more sugar if the fruit is tart.
Serve cold in glass cups or bowls, with a spoon of the juice over each. Brazilians often add a scoop of vanilla ice cream or condensed milk on top.
nt: Don't cook: cut and macerate in juice
Best swap: ripe peaches or cantaloupe for papaya, and lime juice with honey if oranges are not sweet enough.

ing: peeled and cut into short pieces
st: Peel the tough green rind off the cane with a sturdy knife and cut the stalks into pieces about 3 inches long, then into thin strips.
Feed the strips through a cane press or masticating juicer. A bright green-gold, frothy juice will run out.
No juicer: blend the strips with [[0.5 cup]] cold water in a strong blender until pulverized, then squeeze through a cloth-lined strainer.
Stir in the juice of the lime to slow browning and balance the sweetness.
Pour over ice and drink right away, because fresh cane juice darkens and ferments within an hour or so.
nt: Don't cook: press or blend, strain, serve over ice at once
Best swap: no cane, buy frozen sugarcane juice (thaw in the fridge) or 100 percent pressed cane juice from a Latin market.

st: Mix the flour, salt, warm water, [[2 tbsp]] oil and cachaça into a smooth dough. Knead 5 minutes, cover and rest 30 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin, about 1/16 inch, into a large rectangle. Cut into 8 squares of 5 by 5 inches.
Place two slices of mozzarella and a pinch of oregano on one half of each square.
Fold over, press the edges, then seal firmly with a fork so no cheese can leak out.
Heat the oil to 360°F. Fry 2 pastéis at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until golden and blistered.
Drain on paper towels and eat hot.
nt: Best swap: use white vinegar for cachaça at the same amount, or ground beef or hearts of palm for the cheese filling.

st: Cut a large ripe avocado in half, remove the pit, and scoop the flesh into a blender. It should yield easily to a spoon with no brown spots.
Add [[2 cup]] cold milk, [[3 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] lime juice.
Blend on high for 45 seconds until completely smooth and pale green with no streaks of avocado.
Taste and add [[1 tbsp]] more sugar if needed. Brazilians like this quite sweet.
Add the ice and pulse 10 seconds. Pour into tall glasses and drink right away, before it darkens.
nt: Best swap: use oat milk or coconut milk for the milk, and 2 tbsp maple syrup for the sugar.

st: Cook the rice with [[1.75 cups]] water for 18 minutes, rest 10 minutes, and fold in [[3 tbsp]] rice vinegar. Cool to room temperature.
Season the salmon strips and cook them in a pan over medium heat until fully opaque and 145°F inside, about 5 minutes. Cool. Do not use raw fish.
Spread rice over a full nori sheet, leaving a thin border. Lay salmon and cream cheese in a line across the middle and roll tightly.
Roll each log in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing so the crumbs stick.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil to 350°F. Fry the rolls for 2 minutes, turning, until deeply golden. Drain on a rack.
Simmer [[0.25 cup]] soy sauce and [[2 tbsp]] sugar for 3 minutes into a thin glaze. Slice the rolls and drizzle.
nt: Cooked salmon rolled, then deep fried at 350°F
Best swap: bake the rolls at 425°F for 15 minutes, brushed with oil, instead of deep frying.

st: Sift the hydrated tapioca starch through a fine sieve into a bowl so it turns into a dry, fluffy powder. Stir in the salt.
Heat a dry 8 inch nonstick skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes. No oil goes in the pan.
Sprinkle a layer of tapioca about a quarter inch thick across the whole pan, using the sieve for an even layer.
Cook for 1 minute until the grains bind into a white, flexible crepe. Do not stir; the heat fuses the grains.
For the savory version, scatter the cheese over half of the crepe. For the sweet version, add the coconut and a drizzle of condensed milk.
Fold over, cook 30 seconds more until the cheese melts, then slide onto a plate. Brush with butter if you like and eat hot.
nt: Best swap: use plain tapioca starch dampened with 3 tbsp water per cup, rested 15 minutes and sieved, if you cannot find hydrated goma.

st: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line a 10 by 15 inch rimmed baking sheet with greased parchment.
Beat the butter and [[1 cup]] sugar for 4 minutes until pale. Beat in the yolks one at a time, then the vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt together, then fold into the butter mixture until just combined.
Whip the egg whites with the remaining [[0.5 cup]] sugar to stiff, shiny peaks. Fold into the batter in 2 parts.
Spread a thin layer of batter, about 3 mm thick, on the sheet and bake for 8 minutes until lightly golden.
Mix the guava paste with [[2 tbsp]] warm water and microwave 30 seconds to make it spreadable.
Turn the warm sponge onto a sugared towel, peel off the paper and spread with a thin layer of guava. Roll up tightly from the short end.
Repeat with the remaining batter, rolling each new layer around the first, to build a spiral. Cool, wrap and slice with a serrated knife.
nt: Best swap: raspberry jam or dulce de leche for the guava paste, same amount.

st: Rub [[0.75 cup]] butter into [[3 cup]] flour and [[1 tsp]] salt until crumbly. Add the yolks and [[3 tbsp]] cold water and press into a dough. Chill 30 minutes.
Cook the onion in a pan over medium heat 5 minutes until soft. Add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until thick.
Stir in the chicken, hearts of palm, olives and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Pour in [[1 cup]] milk and simmer 5 minutes until creamy. The chicken must be cooked to 165°F. Cool a little.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Press two thirds of the dough into a 9 inch pan, up the sides.
Pour in the filling. Roll the remaining dough, cover the top and pinch the edges. Cut two steam slits.
Brush with a little milk and bake 40 minutes until golden. Rest 15 minutes before cutting.
nt: Best swap: use canned artichoke hearts 1 to 1 in place of hearts of palm; ground beef also works for the chicken.

st: Soak the dried beef in water for 12 hours (or boil it for 30 minutes, changing the water twice) to remove salt, then shred.
Fry the bacon in a large pot over medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp. Add [[2 tbsp]] oil and the shredded beef, and cook 8 minutes until browned.
Add the onion, pepper and garlic and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook 4 minutes until they break down.
Add the rice and stir 2 minutes. Pour in [[4 cup]] hot water and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on low 18 minutes until the rice is tender and moist. Fold in the cilantro and scallions and serve.
nt: Fried, then simmered in one pot
Best swap: use cooked leftover roast beef or corned beef for charque, and cut added salt.
